column1: # Port-only sources: C/C++ the PC port builds for functions that have no byte-exact source it can use.
# Hand-written assembly (the .s stays the matching source; this C is not byte-exact by design),
# compiler-generated C++ code a native C++ compiler doesn't emit the same way, and C++ rewrites of
# matching C (below). Without a row here or in matched.tsv the port runs the translated retail MIPS.
# verify: a test in platform/pc/tests/ (against the retail code), or a matcher (cc/sym/div, as in
# matched.tsv: byte-exact; node tools/check_all.mjs re-verifies those rows too), or `cxx`: C++ class
# members the matching decomp had to spell out as C (raw this+offset access, explicit vptr stores and
# base calls), rewritten as real C++ classes with the same logic (tools/port_cxx.py; not byte-exact,
# the matching C is in git history)
